thread:
Aisha: Quick idea drop A: propose we spin up a Q3 "Tenant Shield" initiative. Aim: deliver a buyer-visible "shield" product (routing + residency guarantees + isolation controls) that sales can attach to contracts. Want a tight scope for an 8-week pilot.
Marco: Love the name. Can we scope a Minimal Viable Shield (MVS)? What must exist for legal to sign "residency"?
Aisha: MVS candidate: 1) routing tags + residency-aware router in dry-run; 2) per-tenant residency flag in deployment API; 3) telemetry: per-tenant region histograms + audit logs; 4) SLA doc and short acceptance checklist. No per-tenant dedicated hardware yet.
Nina: Security notes: KMS scoping and audit trails are musts. Also we should ensure token/key access logs surface in the acceptance checks. Legal will want wording that says "best-effort region-local" unless we can guarantee >99% locality.
Ethan: Infra caveats: KV cache and prefetch are shared. If we namespace cache keys by tenant, hit rates drop ~10-20% in our sim. That affects p95. Alternative is soft isolation with affinity headers and probabilistic fallbacks.
Marco: For the pilot, let's do soft enforcement + dry-run logs so customers can validate behavior without being blocked. After pilot we can consider hard cutover and quota isolation.
Aisha: Acceptance checklist (draft) for pilot customers:
- Step 1: Create tenant with residency=EU and deploy a sample model.
- Step 2: Send synthetic request trace (producer script provided) -> Assert route shows EU-edge path for >95% of requests.
- Step 3: Measure p95 for gen workload with pilot config <= 300ms.
- Step 4: Simulate instance drain (kill agent in a zone) -> Verify fallback respects SLA (latency bump within tolerated window) and logs show eviction decision.
- Step 5: Verify KMS access logs & audit entries for deployment actions.
Nina: Add: verify that exportable audit CSV includes tenant_id, action, actor, timestamp. Legal will want that evidence.
Ethan: Metrics we should gate on for launch: region-local percent >= 95% for residency-tagged traffic, p95 <= 300ms, cold-start rate < 3% during steady load, tenant-isolation incidents = 0 in pilot, and cache-hit delta within acceptable bounds (<20% hit-rate loss).
Marco: Owners: Product= Aisha, Core Routing= Marco, Telemetry= Ethan, Security= Nina, SRE rollouts=Sam (assign later). We'll put these on a tracker.
Aisha: Timeline: Week 0-2: routing dry-run + residency flag in API; Week 3-4: telemetry + audit exports; Week 5-6: pilot onboarding with customer A & B; Week 7-8: analysis and go/no-go.
Ethan: Implementation notes: please avoid per-tenant dedicated pools for this pilot. Use affinity scoring: prefer local nodes but allow fallback to nearest compatible region. We'll expose a feature flag: `shield.enforce_mode` with values `dry-run|soft|hard`.
Marco: UX ask: small "Shield Overview" PDF and a short acceptance checklist for customers + a 1-slide econ slide showing expected cost uplift and recommended surcharge.
Nina: Risk register (initial): 1) Capacity overcommit -> customer latency spikes; 2) Cache namespace perf regression; 3) Legal/regulatory push on absolute residency claims; 4) Unexpected egress cost.
Aisha: Mitigations: 1) limit pilot customers to low-QPS footprints; 2) keep dry-run default; 3) craft conservative residency language for contracts; 4) billing meter to capture egress during pilot.
DevOpsBot: Canary deploy queued: infra/tenant-shield/dry-run -> staging at 2025-06-02T09:30Z
Marco: Experiment plan: toggle two knobs during pilot: `batching.window_ms` and `quant.profile` to measure latency vs cost. We'll run A/B for 48h windows per customer.
Ethan: Also add a small synthetic workload that exercises cold-start patterns so we can measure warmup behavior.
Aisha: Action items: (1) Aisha create GH project + doc; (2) Marco implement routing dry-run and `shield.enforce_mode` flag; (3) Ethan add per-tenant telemetry + audit CSV export; (4) Nina draft KMS audit checklist + legal pre-brief; (5) SRE prep rollback playbook and canary criteria.
Marco: I'll start a PR for the router dry-run today. ETA end of week.
Nina: I'll loop in legal/security and share acceptance wording.
Ethan: I'll prototype telemetry changes and share a sample CSV.
Aisha: Scheduling: let's review progress in next Wed product sync. If we stay on track we can start customer onboarding week 5.
Marco: Great. Keeping scope tight helps. :rocket:
Aisha: Thanks team. I'll post the GH link in ~30m.
